title: Find out why your computer runs hot with an agent
summary: While building a temperature app, a Redditor's Claude Code reportedly traced high heat to a hidden cryptominer using about 1175% CPU and guided its removal.
agent_role: The agent linked odd temperature readings to a background process, found its startup item, and proposed a staged cleanup. The user approved each step and deleted one file by hand.
outcome: Per a news report of the Reddit post, the miner was stopped and quarantined; one file needed manual deletion and a Malwarebytes scan followed.
what_they_did: A Reddit user was building a Mac app to show sensor readings with Claude Code. Temperatures looked too high, so the agent looked at running programs. It found a mining program set to restart at every boot. It then proposed stopping the startup item, ending the process, and moving files to quarantine.
how_it_went: The report says the miner used about 1175% CPU and pushed the chip to 112°C. Most cleanup went through the agent; one file had to be deleted manually. This is a news write-up of one unverified post.
worth_knowing: The agent asked before stopping processes or moving files. The article notes an agent is no substitute for proper security software, and one scan does not prove a machine is clean.
prompt: My [Mac/PC] runs hot and slow even when idle. Check which programs are using the most processor and memory, and list any I may not recognize. Look at startup items and background services for anything unusual. Explain what each suspicious item is and why. Then propose a step-by-step cleanup plan, such as stopping a startup item, ending a process, or moving files to a quarantine folder. Do not stop, move, or delete anything until I approve each step.

curation.rationale: A genuine case of an agent tracing a symptom to hidden malware and guiding cleanup with approval, but it is secondhand news coverage of a single unverified Reddit post.
